% babel's \useshorthands{!}, which makes ! active in the preamble, with
% shorthands to a command made by \NewDocumentCommand (!!) and by
% \newcommand (!+): in the text, in a heading and the table of contents, a
% footnote, a theorem, \emph, \textsf, and \texttt, with hyperref. amsthm
% and hyperref load after \useshorthands, while ! is active. A bare ! stays
% a mark, ! in math is a factorial, also inside a footnote and a heading,
% and ! in verbatim stays literal.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[english]{babel}
\NewDocumentCommand\term{t^ m}{\textit{#2}}
\newcommand\strong[1]{\textbf{#1}}
\useshorthands{!}
\defineshorthand{!!}{\term}
\defineshorthand{!+}{\strong}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\tableofcontents
\section{The !!{bang} heading! Again}
A !!{word} and a mark! Then a !+{strong} one.\footnote{A !!{note} term and a !+{note} too! Yes.}
\begin{theorem}
Every !!{group} has a !+{unit}!
\end{theorem}
In \emph{an !!{emph} term}, \textsf{a !!{sans} term}, and \texttt{a !!{mono} term}.
The factorial $n!$ and
\[ (n+1)! = (n+1)\,n! \]
There are\footnote{as many as $n!$ ways} orders.
\section{Counting $n!$ orders}
Verbatim \verb|a!!b| and
\begin{verbatim}
